message.content:
Bill’s net southward distance is

\[
\frac12+\frac12=1 \text{ mile south}
\]

and his eastward distance is

\[
\frac34 \text{ mile east}.
\]

These two displacements are perpendicular, so the direct-line distance from his starting point is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs \(1\) and \(\frac34\):

\[
d=\sqrt{1^2+\left(\frac34\right)^2}
=\sqrt{1+\frac{9}{16}}
=\sqrt{\frac{25}{16}}
=\frac54
=1.25.
\]

The answer is 1.25.
